## 60e8a302bbab

**Reproduced teaching-distribution defect: every ordinary generated gray line is
SE-oriented, so the shortcut “replace every 5 with 8” fits the generated
sampler although it is not the selected rule.** The audited generator SHA-256
is `d82931f1229213557889f7687b02e11f4c217efa95975593e5c6a2144b74c9e4`;
the executed canonical rule hash is `187f71890685`.

I generated 120 inputs: seeds `1000..1039`, sample indices `0..39`, in each of
`easy`, `medium`, and `hard`. All 120 passed `self_check`; all 120 had at least
one SE adjacency and zero SW adjacencies. Thus every gray cell is recolored 8
by the authority, exactly matching the shortcut. A retained ordinary sample
at seed 17, index 0, medium also matches the shortcut byte-for-byte.

The exact distinguishing input is a 9×9 color-7 grid with an SE line of length
4 at `(0,0)..(3,3)` and an SW line of length 3 at
`(6,8),(7,7),(8,6)`. The authoritative Racket output colors the four SE cells
8 and the three SW cells 2; the shortcut colors all seven cells 8, differing at
the three SW coordinates. The current generator rejects this input solely
because it contains SW pairs, which confirms the distribution restriction
rather than invalidating the authority counterexample.

Evidence: `checks/audit/60e8a302bbab/input.json`,
`checks/audit/60e8a302bbab/racket.json`,
`checks/audit/60e8a302bbab/rival.json`, and
`checks/audit/60e8a302bbab/summary.json`.

Authoritative command, run from the packet root through the Racket wrapper
(effective working directory `repo`):

```sh
python3 run_with_racket.py python3 -m arcpuzzles apply 60e8a302bbab \
  --input ../checks/audit/60e8a302bbab/input.json \
  --out ../checks/audit/60e8a302bbab/racket.json
```

No audited source was changed. A repair should generate both orientations and
examples in which both are present with unequal support; it should also cover
the authority's SE-wins tie behavior or explicitly narrow and document that
domain.
